small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes the full conv MAC inside every pool-window iteration (POOL*POOL=16x redundant work). Swap the loop order: compute each conv output position once, accumulate into the pooled register, instead of recomputing acc per (ki,kj). Also hoist the bias add outside the POOL loop (add once, multiplied by 1, not 16 times).
- Increase BLOCK_OC to 32 or 64 and tile over the pooled spatial dimension with BLOCK_P=32; sweep num_warps in {4,8} and num_stages in {2,3} via triton.autotune. With OC=64 this lets one program cover all output channels and reduce grid contention on the atomic_add.
- Replace the per-element atomic_add with a block-local reduce + single atomic per program (already partially done), and consider eliminating atomics by launching grid=(N,) with the kernel doing the full reduction over (OC, PH*PW) internally when fast_p remains low.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile). Inner loop iterates over IC*KH*KW as the GEMM-K axis using tl.dot on BLOCK_M×BLOCK_K × BLOCK_K×BLOCK_N tiles. After the dot, apply bias, divide by POOL², sigmoid in the epilogue, then block-reduce-sum and atomic_add into out[n]. This uses tensor cores and removes the redundant POOL² conv recomputation.
- Fuse pooling by having each "pooled output" tile gather its POOL×POOL conv outputs in registers: compute conv for an OH×OW tile sized to a multiple of POOL, sum the POOL×POOL groups in-register, sigmoid, then reduce. This materializes the full conv output (satisfies the contract) but never writes it to HBM.
- For the final sum over (OC, PH, PW) per N, use a persistent reduction strategy: each program handles one N and loops over OC/spatial tiles, accumulating a scalar in registers, then a single store to out[n] — avoiding atomic contention entirely.
